name: Lyman Wight
role: Missouri leader and later member of the Twelve
dateNote: Section 52 named him in June 1831, and he was ordained an apostle on 8 April 1841.
importance: Lyman Wight joined in November 1830, and section 52 sends him to Missouri with a warning that Satan desires to sift him. Section 103 sends him to raise volunteers for Zion in 1834. He lived at Adam-ondi-Ahman and was jailed with Joseph Smith in Missouri in 1838–39. Section 124 calls him to preach and help build the Nauvoo House; he later led a group to Texas and was excommunicated in 1848.
connections: He travels with John Corrill, Parley P. Pratt, and Sidney Rigdon. In section 124 he works with George Miller, John Snider, and Peter Haws.

sources.title: Lyman Wight, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: Dates, ordinations, imprisonment, apostleship and excommunication (3 Dec. 1848) checked on JSP; death date read from a cut fragment as 31 Mar. 1858. Bare “Lyman” left out because it also names Lyman Johnson.
